dedupeKey: quality|Exec/RunCommand argv loses its nax-config refusal with no write-refusal backstop|nax-agent/src/tools/package-managers.ts

action.reason: Scope-backed: the PRD's outOfScope names this exact case as explicitly not pinned ('US-003 only: whether Exec (RunCommand with argv) admits a positional ./.nax/config.json under a clean scan is not pinned'). The observed behaviour is the read gate's own semantics propagated, not a bypass: normalizeExec's positional screen consults the injected configRefusal, which is open only under the same configReadable predicate (clean scan AND raw-or-absent Bash) that governs Read/Grep/Glob, so a gated dispatch or any finding keeps the refusal (pinned by the moved test at coding-tool-support-owned-paths.test.ts:170-187). A clean scan means the scanner found nothing in exactly the path set the gate can admit, so no secret is disclosed, and package-manager install verbs treat the positional token as a source — they never write the named file, so .nax/config.json cannot be modified from this branch with or without the OS sandbox.

rationale: Verified in code: resolveWithin is the only screen findPositionalPathConflict uses (package-managers.ts:355-362, policy-paths-branch.ts:102-110), and Exec's argvBranch (policy.ts:191-235) short-circuits before applyPathRules, so writeRefusal is indeed not consulted there — but the branch is gated by the same configReadable the rest of the gate uses (coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:515-546). The residual is a read-tool-equivalent, self-consistent consequence the PRD deliberately left unpinned, and its residual safety (no write to the config; nothing to disclose when the scan is clean) holds. Waiving keeps the spec intact; a blanket Exec refusal would contradict the clean-opens-reads design, and adding an AC would mean superseding a spec line that is still accurate enough to stand.

action.instruction:

1) packages/nax/src/agents/config-read-gate.ts: change NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX to text naming `nax doctor` (e.g. " -- reads are disabled for this dispatch; run `nax doctor` for details."); delete NAX_CONFIG_SECRET_READ_DISABLED_REASON and the third `disabledReason?: string` parameter so the export is the SPEC signature createConfigReadGatePolicy(base: OwnedPathsPolicy, configReadable: boolean): OwnedPathsPolicy, and the closed-gate configRefusal returns `base` refusal + NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX for every config rel (gated/clean, unscannable and rejecting-scan alike), still returning `undefined` where `base` returns `undefined`. Leave NAX_CONFIG_READ_TOOLS, NAX_CONFIG_WRITE_REFUSAL, writeRefusal and bashRefusal behaviour untouched.

2) packages/nax/src/agents/coding-tool-support-resolve.ts (~:48-49, :519-549): drop the NAX_CONFIG_SECRET_READ_DISABLED_REASON import and call createConfigReadGatePolicy(_codingToolSupportDeps.ownedPaths, configReadable) with two arguments, removing the per-caller gated/secret reason string. 4) No other file pins the old text (checked) — src/agents/index.ts already exports only the SPEC's three constants. Re-run the US-003 suites plus test/unit/agents/nax-owned-writes-copy.test.ts and `bun run typecheck` in packages/nax.

rationale: Verified in code: NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX is ' -- reads are disabled for this dispatch.' (no doctor) and the gated-Bash reason is supplied per-caller by coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:546 as 'config reads are unavailable while Bash approval is gated or escalated'; only the scan-dirty case (NAX_CONFIG_SECRET_READ_DISABLED_REASON) names `nax doctor`. SPEC's read-gate table annotates the closed-gate suffix '(names `nax doctor`)', US-003 AC2 requires the suffix to name it, and AC15 requires the gated-Bash Read denial to name it — so the implementation and the two tests that assert not.toContain('nax doctor') under the labels 'US-003 AC2'/'US-003 AC15' contradict explicit ACs. The code also added an unlisted third parameter and unlisted NAX_CONFIG_SECRET_READ_DISABLED_REASON export, deviating from SPEC's new-symbols block. The spec is self-consistent and satisfiable by a string change (no AC conflicts, nothing impossible), so supersede is not warranted; the code's 'doctor is misleading on a clean gated config' preference is a design taste the spec already decided against, and the policy is that a drifted trade-off the spec states is a decision. Fix, not waive: no spec- or scope-backed reason exists for the neutral/secret split, and the caller-supplied reason is exactly the footgun that produced the drift. (Not part of this ruling: the module sits at src/agents/config-read-gate.ts rather than SPEC's nax-config-read-gate.ts — already recorded in the story's repoScopedFixes and cosmetic.)
